sourceInformation.genre: Action-adventure with combat, environmental puzzles and escape
sourceInformation.perspective: Cinematic overhead third-person with a following orthographic camera
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer; TSL cel materials; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; AI Hub Session Protocol v1/client 1.4.0; PeerJS 1.5.5
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded and ink look: faceted sandstone, jade shadows, silhouette outlines and gold accents
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and authored AnimationClips, with procedural whip, roll, grapple and boulder animation
sourceInformation.audio: Original synthesized adventure score at 10% default volume, procedural effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 player host-authoritative co-op through AI Hub shared-world sessions, standalone WebRTC rooms and same-origin BroadcastChannel
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripted full expedition; actual WebGPU runtime; keyboard, emulated standard gamepad and touch; physics and offline audio; two-page co-op; AI Hub normal, latency/loss, host-departure and dedicated-server harness; WebGL fallback screenshots for visual inspection
sourceInformation.research: none; native model knowledge only. The specified AI Hub integration files and runtime dependencies were downloaded for implementation.

testingFeedback: Testing caught 2 issues: a missing transitive Three.js import-map entry and a cosmetic snake-facing mismatch. Integration review also corrected multiplayer result delivery, stable player seats, shared restart and attract-loop edge cases.
1 critical runtime issue: the missing three/webgpu import-map entry prevented the assembled cel-material build from loading. It was fixed and the actual browser harness passed afterward.

The actual AI Hub browser conformance harness was most helpful: it caught the transitive module import failure and verified normal co-op, impaired networking, host departure and a dedicated host without a local player.

The default WebGPU headless screenshot was least helpful: the compositor produced a blank canvas despite a running, error-free game. WebGPU state checks and WebGL engine-fallback screenshots provided useful verification. Physical-controller feel, real-device listening and cross-network WebRTC NAT traversal: unknown; those were tested with the supplied emulation and local-page stand-ins where possible.
engineFeedback: Three.js native animation clips, procedural geometry and TSL node materials made it straightforward to give the whole expedition a consistent illustrated style.
Yes. The TSL build transitively imports three/webgpu, which needed its own import-map entry. WebGPU headless screenshots also required a separate visual inspection path.
The complete adventure framework: character controls, whip combat, trap timing, sign puzzle, checkpoints, host-authoritative shared world, controller menus, attract replay and live developer tuning.
Coordinating input, native animation, Rapier collision and network authority while keeping the single-file build reliable across renderer backends was the hardest part.
none; the engine and physics libraries were not modified. Game-specific materials, animation clips and systems use their public APIs.
Reliable headless WebGPU image capture would make the rendered frame directly inspectable in automated game validation.
promptFeedback: The complete vertical-slice requirements and concrete stand-ins for controller, touch, audio and multiplayer testing made the intended finish line clear.

The no-research instruction sits beside a required online integration URL. I treated downloading that exact protocol implementation and runtime dependencies as implementation work, while doing no source or design research.
Making the expedition, co-op authority, controller focus, touch assists, attract replay and developer tools all work together in a polished single-file package was the hardest part.
Explicitly permit implementation documentation downloads under the no-research rule, and clarify when a dated source refers to a game adaptation rather than its film.

aiHub.name: Raiders of the Lost Fortune
aiHub.description: Whip through a sunken temple, outwit its ancient signs and borrow a priceless idol. Escape its very large return policy alone or with an accomplice.
aiHub.controls: WASD / left stick move; mouse / right stick aim; LMB / Square whip; Space / Cross leap or grapple; Ctrl / Circle roll; E / Triangle interact; Shift / L3 sprint; Esc / Options pause; assisted touch controls.
